rv.q: It could scarcely be more pompous – but happily, there are plenty of entertaining tricks to keep pomp-phobes like myself onside.
Combined with a charismatic cast and a succession of genuinely jaw-dropping moments, the result is a show that understands exactly what its audience wants.
This is a hugely entertaining night out. It knows exactly what it is, it does not pretend to be more, and it delivers wonder with real generosity and craft.
These tricks have been done before and done better, which dampens the overall excitement.
So, it's good family fun, but the team should be aware that not every adult in the show is heterosexual.
It was the most ambitious and jaw dropping spectacle of a magic show I've ever seen and was left many times scratching my head wondering how on earth they managed to pull off those tricks.
An almost perfect production that has so much pageantry and spectacle that the smaller elements are bound to look not as impressive in comparison.
It is a shame that this production offers nothing new and only has the most tenuous of links to a franchise it has shoved a name on for no rhyme or reason.

cn.t: Critics find this high-octane illusion spectacular delivers jaw-dropping magic and family-friendly entertainment, though it bears little resemblance to the film franchise beyond its name. The slick acts and bombastic production mostly dazzle.
